meta.interpreter_note: D4, D6 and D7 depend on str.isalpha(), which the RUNNING INTERPRETER resolves. This fixture is generated on 3.11.13 / unicodedata 14.0.0 — the gateway's own interpreter (/home/gazetteer/miniconda/envs/whg), measured directly from the running process rather than inferred. ⚠ v3 asserted the gateway was 3.9.25 / 13.0.0. That was WRONG: 3.9.25 is the system python on the host, not the interpreter the service runs. The index writer is the same 3.11.13 / 14.0.0, so writer and reader now agree and there is no skew to follow.
meta.quantisation: np.round(unit_vector*127.0).astype(int8) -- matches update_es.quantize_embeddings_to_bytes, NO clip, round-half-to-EVEN
meta.contract: char_ids, script_id, lang_id: EXACT. int8: exact for an fp32 reimplementation; a quantised ONNX client should assert a bound (cos>=0.995, |delta|<=4) -- a tokeniser regression shows up at cos~-0.3, not as rounding.
meta.known_defect_D5: Script ranges are LATER-ENTRY-WINS. FB00-FB17 overlaps Hebrew presentation forms with Armenian ligatures, so U+FB00-FB05 (LATIN ligatures) score ARMENIAN. This is WRONG and is reproduced deliberately: the index was written with it, so correct means identical. Do not 'improve' the scan.
meta.changelog_v3: Added two DISCRIMINATING D6 cases (U+9FFD, U+08B5). The v2 D6 case (U+0870) was decorative: it sits outside every named script range, so it resolves to OTHER whether the alpha filter counts it or not, and a newer-Unicode interpreter still passes it. Found by whg3-da mutating its implementation to \p{L} and observing all 33 cases still pass. Kept and relabelled rather than deleted, so nobody re-adds it believing it tests something.
meta.changelog_v4: Regenerated for Symphonym v8 with the v8 vocabularies. (a) All 35 v3 cases keep their index and order; their char_ids and lang_ids CHANGE because the v8 vocabularies renumber almost everything — of 113,269 shared characters only 98 keep their id. (b) Six D7 cases appended in newly split scripts (Gurmukhi, Myanmar, Ethiopic, Tibetan, Khmer, Lao): these are the ONLY cases that can detect an unported range table, since every v3 case is in a script that existed in v7 and regenerates identically either way. (c) Generated on 14.0.0, not 13.0.0; the D6 expectations and warnings are corrected accordingly.
